title: Our Journey Together: a shared journal for parent and child | Mazo Moon
description: A pass-back-and-forth journal for a grown-up and child: dark pages for you, light pages for them, and pages you fill in together. 113 pages, 6 × 9 in.
card: A journal you pass back and forth.
lead: A shared journal for a grown-up and a child to fill in, pass back and keep.
for: For parents, grandparents, aunties and carers who want a little more connection
For children who find it easier to write it down than to say it out loud
For busy weeks when proper chats are hard to find

p: You know there’s more going on in their head. But the questions you ask at teatime get one-word answers, and the big conversations seem to happen at bedtime when everyone’s tired.
It isn’t that they don’t want to share. Talking face to face can just feel like a lot.

approach.h: Pass a book back and forth instead
p: Dark pages are for you, light pages are for your child, and pages marked TOGETHER are for both of you. Fill in your page, then leave the journal somewhere for them to find: under a pillow, in a drawer, on the stairs.
There’s no pressure and no right way to do it. Over time it becomes a slow conversation on paper that you’ll both want to keep.

offer.h: A quiet way to get to know each other better
offer.p: Light, playful prompts on every page, so it never feels like an interview.
features: Dark pages for the grown-up, light pages for the child, so everyone has their own say.
A family tree to draw, and lists to tick and compare, like “Yes, please! or No, thanks!”
Top places you’ve visited, who you’d be if you were a cartoon, what you love right now.

proof.p: Have a look at both sides: the dark grown-up pages and the light pages for your child.
note: I made this journal for the conversations that are hard to start. Some children say far more with a pen than they ever would across the dinner table.
I kept the questions light on purpose. The deeper stuff tends to come out on its own once you’ve both got into the habit.

items: A welcome page explaining how it works, with space for both your names
Dark pages with questions for the grown-up
Light pages with questions for the child
TOGETHER pages, including a family tree to draw
Lists, postcards, speech bubbles and fill-in prompts
113 pages in total, on cream paper

decision.h: One book for the two of you
points: One paperback book, printed and posted by Amazon.
No subscription and nothing to download. Open it and start.
Amazon handles delivery and returns, just like anything else you buy there.

faq: It works best from around seven, once your child can write a few sentences on their own. Younger children can draw their answers or tell you what to write.
Does it have to be a parent?
Not at all. It works for any grown-up and child: grandparents, step-parents, aunties, uncles, godparents or carers.
Do we have to do it in order?
No. Pick any page you like. The only rule is that you pass it back when you’re done.
What if my child doesn’t want to write much?
That’s fine. Many pages can be answered with a tick, a word or a drawing. The point is the connection, not the handwriting.
Yes, it makes a thoughtful gift for a birthday or Christmas, or for a grandparent who lives far away to post back and forth.

close.p: Write the first page tonight and leave it under their pillow.
